articles.title_orig: Live Updates: Houthis launch new attack on Saudi capital as Trump mulls U.S. role in Mideast war's new front
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: Houthis launch new attack on Saudi capital as Trump mulls U.S. role in Mideast war's new front
articles.content_orig:
The escalating war between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces is cutting off lifesaving food supplies to about 800,000 people in the region, according to the U.N. World Food Programme .
Many parts of Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, which is located in Houthi-controlled territory, is completely inaccessible to the nonprofit, the WFP said. There are more than 600,000 people, including 200,000 women and children, in Taiz who depend on humanitarian aid, according to the agency.
"We are critically concerned about the escalating conflict, but even more so about the growing number of people we can no longer reach because of it," El-Khidir Daloum, WFP representative and country director in Yemen, said in a statement Wednesday. "Many of the families affected have been displaced multiple times and were already struggling to afford even basic food items. This is the kind of situation that can rapidly spiral into a humanitarian catastrophe if assistance cannot move safely and reach those who need it most."
The hunger situation in Yemen is among the worst in the world. Ten out of 16 districts in Yemen are categorized as being at emergency levels of food insecurity, the WFP said. About 500,000 children in Yemen under the age of 5 suffer from severe acute malnutrition, according to the group.
There are also 37 WFP employees currently being held by the Houthis, the group said, calling for their immediate release.
The chairman of Saudi Arabia's General Entertainment Authority on Wednesday said the exhibition Six Kings Slam tennis tournament has been postponed for logistical reasons, after Yemen's Houthis carried out several deadly attacks on the kingdom.
"The Six Kings Slam tournament has been postponed due to logistical reasons and will now take place on December 27," wrote Turki Alalshikh on X, sharing a statement from the Riyadh Season entertainment program.
The tournament, while not officially sanctioned as an ATP event, features some of the top players in the world vying for millions of dollars and airs live on Netflix. It had initially been scheduled to air Oct. 21 to 24.
The men's-only event features Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz, Alex De Minaur and Learner Tien, who replaced Jannik Sinner due to injury.
The event premiered in 2024 with Sinner winning each of the first two competitions. Sinner, Alcaraz, Djokovic or Zverev has won every major since Wimbledon in 2022.
Israel has signed a deal with the Pentagon to acquire 12 Apache helicopters from Boeing, according to the Israeli Ministry of Defense.
"The procurement of Apache helicopters is a critical step in building the IDF's force capabilities; it will strengthen operational readiness against a wide range of threats and contribute to the security of the State of Israel for years to come," Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said in a statement.
The helicopters, the newest Apache E model, can carry 16 HELLFIRE missiles, 76 2.75-inch rockets and 1,200 30 mm chain gun rounds, according to Boeing.
While the deal was signed Wednesday, it will be awhile before they are in combat. They are "scheduled for delivery early next decade," according to the Israeli defense ministry. Israel already has older models of the Apache helicopter.
Israel agreed to buy a second squadron of F-15IA fighter jets from Boeing earlier this year. They initially purchased a squadron in 2024.
Kevin Hassett, the White House's top economic adviser, blamed the disappointing inflation numbers for September on attacks against Saudi oil assets.
"What happened was that because the Houthis started attacking the Saudi pipeline and other Iranian proxies from Iraq were attacking refineries and so on, we had a negative shock to energy again in September," Hassett told Fox Business on Wednesday.
"A lot of Trump policies are helping to keep inflation down, but the energy shock is really the headline story today," he said.
Hassett said much of the energy concerns had "abated," and while the East-West pipeline is back up and running, the Houthis have also stepped up attacks in Saudi Arabia. In addition to targeting civilian airports, they have targeted Aramco, the world's largest oil producer, facilities and even the executive headquarters overnight Wednesday.
The price of Brent crude, the international standard for oil, was hovering around $105 on Wednesday, up from $98 on the last day of September.
Saudi Arabia plans to move ahead with a major investment conference in Riyadh despite Houthi attacks on the kingdom, offering on-site and virtual attendance as well as alternative air and land travel routes, diplomatic sources told AFP.
Riyadh usually hosts a packed calendar of events, but it has recently seen escalating military tensions with the Iran-backed Yemeni group, which has intensified attacks on the kingdom's airports and oil facilities.
Saudi Arabia's Future Investment Initiative Institute hosts an annual forum dubbed "Davos in the desert," which usually draws foreign leaders and business titans, and this year it is scheduled to be held in Riyadh from Oct. 26 to 29.
In order to prevent cancellation, organizers reached out to embassies and foreign companies to explore "hybrid" participation options, allowing officials and business executives to attend either in person or virtually, diplomatic sources said.
They have even discussed arrangements for participants to fly by private jet to Dhahran airport in eastern Saudi Arabia before traveling by road to Riyadh.
A diplomat from an Asian country said "they contacted us and offered that attendees travel to Manama or Doha," referring to the capitals of Bahrain and Qatar respectively, and then drive by land to the Saudi capital.
Riyadh's international airport, a main target for Houthi attacks, suspended operations last week after 13 were killed in a strike there, with no clear timeline for when air traffic would reopen.
Inflation accelerated across the U.S. in September, rising at an annual rate of 3.7% as energy prices soared, according to new government data.
Inflation picked up after two months of holding steady at an annual pace of 3.4%. Core CPI, which excludes the more volatile energy and gas categories, rose 2.6% from a year ago, accelerating from a 2.4% rate in August and higher than economists' forecast of 2.5%.
Inflation has risen sharply since the start of the year due to soaring energy prices, sparked by the war in Iran and Russia's war with Ukraine.
The Labor Department said Wednesday that gasoline prices, which rose 9.1% in September from the prior month, accounted for more than half the monthly increase in the CPI report. Energy prices rose 20.4% from a year ago, while gasoline jumped 34.2%.
Prices at the pump have cooled slightly in recent weeks but remain elevated. The national average for a gallon of gasoline was $4.33 a gallon on Wednesday, AAA reported, up from $2.98 before the war started. The national average for diesel, which hit a record high in late September, was $6.29 a gallon.
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun received a call from Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday to discuss the situation in the Middle East, according to the Lebanese president's office.
Both sides "discussed the current situation in the region in light of recent developments and agreed on the necessity of supporting diplomatic solutions as the best means to put an end to the conflicts in the region," the Lebanese presidency said in a statement about the call.
The Iran-backed Hezbollah militant group has been waging war with Israel in the southern part of Lebanon for months, with the official Lebanese government attempting to cool the conflict down with ceasefire agreements. Those have all been dismissed and ignored by Hezbollah.

articles.title_orig: UK’s ‘incoherent’ approach to China plagued by a lack of expertise, report says
articles.title_zh: UK’s ‘incoherent’ approach to China plagued by a lack of expertise, report says
articles.content_orig:
International grouping of China-sceptic legislators warns of risks inherent in misjudging bilateral relationship
The UK’s approach to China is “beset by incoherence” and plagued by a lack of senior expertise, according to a report warning of the risks inherent in misjudging the bilateral relationship.
Wednesday’s audit by the Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China (Ipac), an international grouping of China-sceptic legislators, says past engagement with Beijing has often exposed the UK to the risks of interference without delivering the opportunities promised.
“Successful UK engagement with China must always be framed by an understanding that the PRC (People’s Republic of China) is an inherently hostile authoritarian state that does not share our values,” an underlined sentence in the audit reads.
The inherent power imbalance in the relationship with the world’s second largest economy is “further compounded by muddled policy and weak engagement”, it says.
It cites the example of a visiting Chinese delegation who had noted that no one who engaged with Beijing at a senior level in government was a Mandarin speaker, or had significant experience of living in China.
Although British expertise exists, it is often siloed and “not translated into capability”, Ipac, which counts members from all the UK’s major parties, says.
In an endorsement, the former security minister Tom Tugendhat said the report was “a clear-eyed and realistic take on the defining foreign policy problem of this century, filling a gap left by years of policy neglect”.
While the report accepts that “disengagement was not an option”, it advocates for clearly defined red lines around issues such as critical infrastructure, frontier technologies, and human rights.
The document offers several recommendations, including better institutional coordination, the strengthened use of national security tools, and diversification of supply chains.
It identifies emerging technologies such as AI as posing new challenges, in terms of disinformation and surveillance capabilities.
The climate crisis is identified as a low-risk area for cooperation and alignment.
“Climate targets as set will not be met without cooperation with China, and accepting medium term dependence. This means accepting supply chains tainted by forced labour and unfair trade practices,” the audit says.
The Guardian has contacted the UK government and the Chinese embassy in London for comment.
It was “very welcome” that there was an understanding that better language skills were needed to deal with China, said Kerry Brown, a former diplomat and director of the Lau China Institute at King’s College London.
However, he said, “the critical issue now is lived experience” in China.
“Some of the members of Ipac … are really keen on promoting this very security-oriented idea that going to China is in some ways opening you up to exposure,” he said.
“You can’t teach really important things in a classroom;, you can only go and learn them through daily life … and that is the thing that is very difficult to do now, and it’s also the thing that doesn’t seem to be supported.”

articles.title_orig: Inflation jumps to 3.7% as gas and diesel prices squeeze consumers ahead of the midterms
articles.title_zh: Inflation jumps to 3.7% as gas and diesel prices squeeze consumers ahead of the midterms
articles.content_orig:
Prices rose across broad swaths of the U.S. economy in September, as high energy costs triggered by the Iran war pushed up prices in many major consumer categories.
The Bureau of Labor Statistics said Wednesday that overall prices rose 3.7% from a year ago, and 0.6% from August. Categories including housing, clothing and restaurant and take out food all saw price increases. Only three major categories saw price declines: groceries, medical care commodities and utility gas service.
“The index for gasoline rose 9.1 percent in September, accounting for over half of the monthly all items increase,” the BLS said in its report.
The report adds to ongoing concerns that persistent inflation is taking a toll on consumers, particularly as wage growth has been stagnant. As of September, the growth in wages was pacing at 3% on an annual basis. Paychecks have not grown faster than inflation since March.
The overall increase was slightly more than had been expected by economists polled by Dow Jones, who forecast a jump to 3.6%.
Core inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, also rose to 2.6% from a year ago, or 0.3% from August. This was also slightly more than had been expected.
Friday’s number is the final inflation report before November’s pivotal midterm elections, in which business owners and consumers have said they will be voting with their bottom line in mind.
“This was a disappointing number,” said Kevin Hassett, chairman of the White House Council of Economic Advisers, on Fox Business Network. Still, he maintained that “a lot of Trump policies are helping to keep inflation down.”
Since August, oil prices have risen to more than $106 per barrel from about $80. The price of unleaded gas, which most consumers use, has risen 45% since late February, when the United States and Israel launched the Iran war. The price of diesel, which powers businesses, farms, the shipping industry and other critical sectors, has soared 70% over the same period.
As early voting kicks off this week, the data also comes at a precarious moment for Republicans defending majorities in the House and the Senate. Polls consistently find that inflation and the high cost of living are top issues this year for voters in both parties.
Stocks fell sharply Wednesday. Before the data, market odds showed that traders had expected the Federal Reserve to wait until December to raise rates. After the data, odds rose above 55% for an October hike.
As of midday Wednesday, the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.2% and the S&P 500 tumbled 0.8%. The Russell 2000 index, which tracks small and medium sized companies, slid 1.5%. The stocks that sold off the most were interest-rate sensitive, such as those in the technology and industrial sectors, which are involved in the ever-expanding AI data center buildout.
The prospect of a rate hike also helped send bond yields higher, which will in turn raise consumer borrowing costs, especially for mortgages. The 10-year yield, which has more influence over consumer rates than other bonds, rose to its highest level since last week.
A Fed rate hike could add even more pressure to consumers, raising the cost of other forms of credit such as credit cards, personal loans and vehicle loans.
The artificial intelligence boom also reared its head last month, as categories that track the price of computers, software and accessories posted record year-over-year price increases.
Ahead of Wednesday’s report, economists had been watching recent price hikes on Apple products and whether they have an impact on the overall inflation figure. The smartphone category rose 0.4% month over month.
Airline fares were also being closely watched, given soaring jet fuel costs. Prices in that category rose 0.2% from August, posting their smallest increase since June.
Despite elevated prices and consumers who say they are being stretched to the limit, data shows that spending has remained strong.
On Wednesday, Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan said that customers continued to spend at a pace 5% higher than last year.
“While much has been made of the AI boom, the consumer is still driving much” of the economy’s momentum, Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser said Tuesday.
Steve Kopack is a senior reporter at NBC News covering business and the economy.

articles.title_orig: Container ship sinks in Strait of Hormuz as Iran steps up attacks
articles.title_zh: Container ship sinks in Strait of Hormuz as Iran steps up attacks
articles.content_orig:
A container ship sank in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday as Iran escalated its attacks on commercial vessels.
The GFS Pride, registered in Singapore, sank after it was struck by an unidentified projectile and caught fire. The ship's 21 crew members were safely evacuated and no injuries were reported, according to the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore .
"Such attacks are unprovoked, unjustifiable and a breach of international law," the Singapore maritime authority said in a statement Wednesday.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed early Wednesday that a container ship exploded and sank after hitting a naval mine, according to the state news agency Tasnim . But there is no independent evidence to confirm that a mine is what caused the Pride to sink, according to the maritime security firm Marisks.
Iran's claims are "consistent with an ongoing psychological operations campaign aimed at generating fear, increasing uncertainty and discouraging commercial shipping" in Hormuz, Marisks said in a security alert.
Iran has escalated its strikes on commercial ships transiting Hormuz in recent weeks, as it tries to choke off a rebound in crude oil exports through the strait.
More than 20 vessels, mostly oil tankers, have come under attack this month in Hormuz, the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman, according to incident reports from the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre.
The attacks this month have left two sailors missing and 12 injured, according to the International Maritime Organization, a United Nations' agency.
Crude oil exports through Hormuz hit prewar levels in September as the U.S. military guided tankers through the strait, but shipments have since pulled back as attacks have increased.
Crude exports through Hormuz averaged 8.5 million barrels per day (bpd) in the week ended Oct. 12, nearly 40% below normal levels before the Iran war, according to data from Kpler .
Shipments from the entire region, including pipelines to the Gulf of Oman and Red Sea, stood at 14 million bpd, or nearly 20% below prewar levels, the data showed.
Daily flows are volatile, with only 3 million barrels of crude transiting Hormuz on Monday while 6 million barrels passed through the strait on Friday, according to Kpler.

articles.title_orig: Cardinal Tagle reads Pope Leo's homily to bishops: 'The world has no future without strong families'
articles.title_zh: Cardinal Tagle reads Pope Leo's homily to bishops: 'The world has no future without strong families'
articles.content_orig:
Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, pro-prefect of the Dicastery for Evangelization, celebrates a Mass in St. Peter's Square at the Vatican Oct. 14, 2026, on the final day of a meeting in which the presidents of bishops' conferences marked the 10th anniversary of "Amoris Laetitia" ("The Joy of Love"). The Mass also included special prayers for the health of Pope Leo XIV following his lung surgery the previous day and diagnosis of cancer. (OSV News/Reuters/Stoyan Nenov)
Send your thoughts to Letters to the Editor . Learn more
Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, the newly elected dean of the College of Cardinals, presided over the closing Mass for the Vatican meeting of bishops on marriage and family on Oct. 14, reading aloud a homily that had been prepared by Pope Leo XIV prior to his lung cancer surgery, saying, "The world has no future without strong families."
Leo had been scheduled to preside over the closing Mass in St. Peter's Square himself before he shocked the world on Sunday with the announcement that he would be having surgery. As a result, the morning Mass took place without the presence of the pope, just hours after the Vatican announced that late Oct. 13 that the surgery had confirmed a diagnosis of lung cancer for the 71-year-old pope.
Participants in the Oct. 7-14 gathering of the world’s bishops’ conference presidents and the heads of Eastern Catholic churches marking the 10th anniversary of Pope Francis' document on the family, Amoris Laetitia , prayed for Leo's recovery in the Prayer of the Faithful during the Mass and listened to the words that the pope had prepared for them.
"The world has no future without strong families open to the gift of children and attentive to their education and growth," Leo wrote in his homily, which emphasized the important role of families in educating and forming the young in the virtues.
The pope highlighted, quoting Amoris in part, that "the importance of the virtues, among which a special place is given to chastity, which is 'invaluable for the genuine growth of love between persons,'" in preparing young people for true love in marriage.
"Marriage preparation programs conscientiously developed for this purpose in parishes and pastoral areas are commendable. Yet such courses alone are insufficient, for they must be preceded and supported by an education in love that accompanies a person’s growth from childhood," he wrote.
Leo highlighted Francis' post-synodal apostolic exhortation that followed the Synod on the Family, saying that "marriage preparation begins at birth."
"In this way, love lived within the family — with its moments of struggle, mistakes and failures, yet also with the marvel of its unpredictable, everyday life — becomes the first school of human affection, the first precious and irreplaceable apprenticeship in the 'joy of love,'" Leo said.
Leo said that "the values of openness to life and respect for life, from conception to natural death, are also rooted in this charity, which is fundamental to our existence and to our life together as human beings."
"The family is the foremost guardian of these values, a beacon for the good of humanity," he added.
As Tagle read aloud the pope's prepared homily, the cardinal noted the presence of Patriarch Paul III Nona, the patriarch of Baghdad of the Chaldeans, whom Leo granted ecclesiastical communion in April.
"I myself have the honor of presiding over this celebration by special mandate of His Holiness Pope Leo XIV, in order to manifest publicly the ecclesiastical communion he has granted to His Beatitude Paul III Nona, Patriarch of Baghdad of the Chaldeans, who is participating in this Eucharist," the cardinal said.
"Your Beatitude, your presence helps us better understand our identity as the Church, which is a communion in Christ the Lord of the Churches of various rites and traditions, in a unity that is expressed tangibly with the Successor of Peter," he added.
The Vatican did not provide an update on Leo's clinical condition in the morning following the announcement of his cancer diagnosis, other than that the pope's first night in the hospital passed calmly.
Following the closing Mass, the bishops, families and experts taking part in the Amoris Laetitia meeting are scheduled to meet again in the late afternoon for the presentation of the meeting's synthesis report at the closing session of the weeklong event.
Due to the personal request of Leo prior to his surgery, the meeting's final synthesis report will no longer be made public on Oct. 14. Jesuit Fr. Giacomo Costa, a consultant to the General Secretariat of the Synod, said that the pope requested to postpone the meeting's final report, noting that Leo "wanted to listen to it and be able to offer his own word on it himself."

articles.title_orig: A New World of Lung Cancer Therapy Awaits Pope Leo
articles.title_zh: A New World of Lung Cancer Therapy Awaits Pope Leo
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
This article was originally published on October 13, 2026, and is being republished by The Independent after the Pope was diagnosed with lung cancer .
Pope Leo will undergo surgery in the coming days to remove a lung nodule that was detected during a routine check-up. The 71-year-old said the growth was “well contained” and spotted early.
So what exactly is a lung nodule, and what’s the link with cancer ?
Lung nodules are small growths found in the spongy tissue of the lungs. They are no more than 3 centimetres in diameter, and can be round or irregularly shaped. Anything larger is referred to as a mass.
Lung nodules are usually detected by imaging of the chest, often using an X-ray or a computed tomography (CT) scan. While some people undergo screening specifically for lung nodules due to their increased risk of cancer, many nodules are picked up incidentally from unrelated scans.
Lung nodules are very common. In a study of 10,431 non-smoking (never or former smoking) participants given a chest CT scan in the northern Netherlands, 37.7% of women and 47.5% of men had at least one lung nodule.
In the United States, lung nodules are detected in 31% of chest CT scans.
The Australian National Lung Screening program suggests that lung nodules will be found in up to half of all people screened, but that most are neither symptomatic nor cancer-related.
As imaging technology improves, and scans are performed more often, more lung nodules are likely to be detected.
Older people, those who smoke, people with a family history of lung cancer and those exposed to asbestos are more likely to have lung nodules.
Fortunately, most lung nodules are harmless. Around 95% of lung nodules tend to be benign (non-cancerous), and are instead caused by factors such as infections, immune-related diseases, and genetic abnormalities.
However, in rare cases (3.7–5.5%), lung nodules may represent the early stages of lung cancer.
A major challenge for clinicians is deciding which nodules are likely to be harmless (or benign), and which are likely to be cancerous and require removal.
Risk assessment considers factors such as the nodule size, density and location, as well as the patient’s age, smoking status and family history of cancer.
It’s also important to refer to any previous medical imaging to detect whether nodule size or characteristics have changed.
Sarah Diepstraten is a Senior Research Officer, Blood Cells and Blood Cancer Division, WEHI (Walter and Eliza Hall Institute of Medical Research).
John (Eddie) La Marca is a Senior Research Officer, Blood Cells and Blood Cancer, WEHI (Walter and Eliza Hall Institute of Medical Research).
This article was first published by The Conversation and is republished under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article .
In some cases, a biopsy of the nodule may also be performed.
Many tools are also being developed to help clinicians make these decisions, including machine learning, as a potential way to help determine whether a nodule is likely to be malignant.
Biomarkers, such as proteins in the blood, or gene expression of surrounding lung cells, are also being investigated as ways to improve decision-making.
If a nodule is causing pain or other symptoms, is growing rapidly, or is determined to be a high risk for cancer, it may be removed surgically.
There are a few ways to remove the nodule.
Open-lung surgery involves making an incision between the ribs to access the lungs.
Other, less-invasive surgeries involve smaller chest incisions that allow a camera and surgical tools to access the lung. A surgeon can then cut out the nodule, either directly or with robotic assistance.
If a nodule is confirmed to be cancerous after removal, then follow-up treatment may be recommended to ensure the cancer hasn’t spread.
The risk of the cancer returning after the cancerous nodule is removed depends on the particular type of lung cancer diagnosed. One study on early-stage, non-small cell lung cancer showed the risk of cancer recurrence was 6–10% for the first four years after surgery, and then decreased to 2% per year.
The risk of developing a new lung cancer remained at 3–6% and did not change over time.
This is compared to a 0.055% chance of developing lung cancer per year in the general population (55 cases per 100,000 people per year).
Lung cancer remains the most deadly form of cancer in Australia, as it is usually detected at a late stage, when treatment is very difficult. It is hoped that the new National Lung Cancer Screening program will help to detect lung cancer early in those at high risk.
If you have concerns, speak to your doctor.

More than 700 startup CEOs, investors, innovators, and healthcare industry leaders from across the U.S. and around the world will convene in Chicago on October 20 for the region's flagship startup and industry innovation conference.
CHICAGO , Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- World Business Chicago (WBC) today announced the keynote speakers and initial program for the inaugural Chicago Venture Summit: Future of Health , taking place October 20 in Chicago's Fulton Market District. The first Chicago Venture Summit dedicated to healthcare and life sciences will convene more than 700 startup CEOs, investors, innovators and industry executives from across the country and around the world to examine the technologies, companies and investment driving the future of health—and Chicago's growing role in shaping it.
"Healthcare and life sciences are industries where Chicago has a clear right to win," said Abin Kuriakose, Chief Strategy and Innovation Officer at World Business Chicago. "We have the talent, research institutions, healthcare systems, corporate leaders, and capital to turn breakthrough ideas into companies that grow and scale. The Chicago Venture Summit brings those pieces together—connecting entrepreneurs and investors while showcasing why Chicago continues to attract investment and drive innovation across the sector."
Together, these leaders bring distinct perspectives from across healthcare, life sciences, investment, and innovation - and each underscores why Chicago is an important place to build, invest, and shape the future of health.
The Chicago Venture Summit: Future of Health will bring together senior leaders shaping the future of healthcare, technology, and innovation — spanning Chicago's healthcare and business communities and our global connections, including leaders from World Business Chicago board companies Health Care Service Corporation and Bank of America:
The Chicago Venture Summit: Future of Health reflects the strength of an ecosystem built on collaboration — connecting healthcare, research, business, investment and global partners. Leaders across that ecosystem share why Chicago has both the talent and the opportunity to help shape the future of health and healthcare:
" Chicago has a remarkable opportunity to shape the future of health by bringing together world-class research, clinical expertise and a growing community of entrepreneurs and innovators," said Rush President and CEO Dr. Omar Lateef. "The Chicago Venture Summit Future of Health reflects the power of that ecosystem and our shared commitment to turning breakthrough ideas into solutions that improve health, advance equity and strengthen communities."
"Health Care Service Corporation (HCSC) is committed to supporting the innovators who are reimagining how we deliver and experience health care," said Dr. Opella Ernest, President, HCSC, and World Business Chicago board member. "Innovation is essential to improving health outcomes and expanding access to care for people of all ages, and Chicago is uniquely positioned to lead that work. By bringing together entrepreneurs, investors, health care leaders and the broader business community, we can help turn bold ideas into solutions that make a meaningful difference for people and communities."
"Canada and the American Midwest share a deep commitment to innovation and an extraordinary concentration of talent, research and entrepreneurial energy," said Claire Kennedy, Consul General of Canada in Chicago. "By strengthening connections between our health care, research, investment and startup communities, we can accelerate the development and commercialization of new ideas across North America. The Chicago Venture Summit: Future of Health is an important opportunity to build those connections and demonstrate what is possible when Canadian and Midwestern innovators work together."
Learn more about the Chicago Venture Summit: Future of Health agenda and official startup portfolio at: https://worldbusinesschicago.com/chicago-venture-summit/
The Chicago Venture Summit: Future of Health is part of World Business Chicago's broader innovation and venture strategy, which also includes programs such as Startup Chicago, Chicago Day at SXSW, ThinkChicago, and previous Chicago Venture Summits, including the Future of Food, Future of Climate Tech, and Future of Logistics. Led by World Business Chicago and supported by our official partners, the October 20, 2026, summit is invite-only. To learn more, please email Helena Gittelman, Director of Innovation, World Business Chicago, at [email protected] .
In collaboration with the Chicago Biomedical Consortium (CBC), World Business Chicago serves as an official Supporting Partner for the Midwest BioBuilder's Summit on November 12, 2026. Led by the CBC, the Summit connects academics, entrepreneurs, and startups with investors, operators, and industry leaders who can help advance their innovations. With a pronounced emphasis on life sciences and biotechnology investment, the BioBuilders Summit echoes the Midwest's industrial spirit, highlighting companies and platforms dedicated to translating breakthroughs into market-ready products and building the infrastructure needed for the next era of biotechnology. You can learn more at www.chicagobiomedicalconsortium.org .
In collaboration with WBC board member University of Illinois System, the Grainger Engineering Tech Startup Challenge, hosted by The Grainger College of Engineering at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, will be held during the Chicago Venture Summit on October 20. Bringing together engineering-powered startups from leading universities across the Midwest and beyond, the competition provides entrepreneurs with a live stage to pitch their ventures to prominent investors, entrepreneurs, and industry leaders in Chicago's thriving tech ecosystem. Participants compete for significant funding while gaining direct exposure to networks and capital. The Challenge reflects The Grainger College of Engineering's commitment to translating cutting-edge research into real-world impact and to positioning the Midwest as a hub for the next generation of deep tech innovation. You can learn more via https://landuyt.illinois.edu/programs/tech-startup-challenge .
As part of the Chicago Venture Summit: Future of Health, World Business Chicago collaborated with Summit Innovation Partner APCO on a new economic-development perspective examining a critical challenge facing health innovation: why proven solutions can still struggle to reach the people and markets they are designed to serve.
" Approval Is the Easy Part: Why Proven Health Innovations Still Stall " explores what it takes to move innovation beyond approval and into adoption, scale and impact. articles.title_orig: China’s Exports Soar, Putting Its Trade Surplus on Track for a Record
articles.title_zh: China’s Exports Soar, Putting Its Trade Surplus on Track for a Record
articles.content_orig:
China’s exports surged by more than one-third in September, a boost to the world’s second-largest economy as it faces slowing growth.
Exports grew by 36.3 percent last month year-on-year to reach $447.18bn, accelerating from a 25 percent gain in August, government figures released on Wednesday show.
The leap marked the biggest monthly rise in exports since 2021, when China’s trade figures were skewed by the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and stringent lockdowns.
Tech-related trade led the growth, with semiconductor exports surging more than 108 percent and shipments of automatic data processing machines jumping nearly 55 percent.
Imports increased 31 percent year-on-year, up from 28.2 percent in August, according to the figures from the General Administration of Customs.
“High-tech demand, supported by the global and domestic AI upcycle, remained the key driver, while China’s pricing and supply-chain competitiveness in other major export categories also helped sustain the momentum,” Taylor Wang, an economist at HSBC in Hong Kong, said in a note to clients.
China’s total exports in the first nine months of the year rose 21.3 percent to $3.37 trillion, while imports gained 27.5 percent to $2.43 trillion.
The gap between exports and imports in the first three quarters gave China a trade surplus of $938.1bn.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) was China’s biggest export market by a wide margin, with exports rising more than 52 percent in September to $81.7bn.
Exports to the European Union rose 25.3 percent in September to $60.15bn, while shipments to the United States jumped 39.6 percent to $47.88bn.
After decades of relying on state-led investment and exports to power its economy, China is striving to find new avenues for growth amid a falling population, deflating property market, and weak domestic consumption, which contributes far less to gross domestic product (GDP) than in advanced economies.
China’s economy is expected to grow 4.5 percent in 2026, according to the International Monetary Fund’s latest growth outlook, which would be the slowest expansion since 1990, excluding the outlier years of the COVID pandemic.
“The strong export growth should keep China’s growth on track to achieve its growth target of 4.5-5 percent for 2026,” Lynn Song, chief economist for Greater China at ING, told Al Jazeera.
“Nonetheless, growth remains quite unbalanced, with domestic data quite soft in comparison,” Song said.
“It will be important to rebalance growth over the medium term if China is to achieve its longterm growth targets.”

articles.title_orig: Pope Leo slept well after cancer surgery, but recovery could take ‘longer than expected’
articles.title_zh: Pope Leo slept well after cancer surgery, but recovery could take ‘longer than expected’
articles.content_orig:
VATICAN CITY — Pope Leo XIV’s recovery from cancer surgery could take “longer than expected,” the president of Peru warned Wednesday, as the leader of the Roman Catholic Church continued to mend at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital.
Keiko Fujimori, in an interview on Peruvian television, said the pace of the pope’s  recovery could determine whether Leo makes his week-long apostolic visit to Peru, which was supposed to start on Nov. 11.
“I want the pope to know that here in Peru, millions of us are praying for his speedy recovery,” Fujimori said. “We will also be watching for any announcements from the Vatican, because we understand that his recovery will take several weeks longer than expected and, therefore, we also understand that there could be some changes to the schedule of his visit.”
Leo, who is a Chicago native , spent more than two decades working in Peru and maintains close ties to that South American country.
Fujimori’s announcement was somewhat at odds with the Vatican’s assertion on Wednesday that the pope was  recovering as expected after a surgery that saw part of his right lung removed and a confirmed cancer diagnosis .
The medical team taking care of the 71-year-old pontiff said he had undergone routine blood tests and a chest X-ray and that, so far, the results “confirm a normal post-operative course: the values are within the expected range for the type of procedure performed.”
The Holy Father has begun walking around his hospital room and ate both breakfast and lunch, they said.
But so far, Leo’s doctors have given no indication that the pontiff might need any further treatment. And the Vatican has not indicated whether the cancer might have spread.
Leo was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma, a type of non-small cell lung cancer, after doctors examined the nodule they had removed from his right lung.
Non-small cell lung cancer accounts for 80% of all cases of the disease, according to the American Lung Association.
Leo spent a calm night in the hospital after surgery to remove a malignant lung nodule was completed “successfully, on schedule and as planned,” the Vatican said Tuesday. Leo was in the operating room for nearly three hours, it said.
The initial lump was detected during a routine check, the Vatican has said. The leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics took the rare step of revealing the health issue — the first of his papacy — during his Sunday noon prayer.
Leo waved to crowds outside Rome’s Gemelli hospital as he entered Tuesday.
The procedure was led by Dr. Stefano Margaritora, Gemelli’s chief thoracic surgeon, with medical staff reciting the rosary prayer in the hospital chapel as the operation began.
The surgery saw the lower lobe of the pope’s right lung removed using a “video-assisted technique,” according to the Vatican.
Following his surgery, the pontiff “woke up normally and, after a brief period of observation, returned to his room on the tenth floor,” the Vatican said. The room is next to the usual papal apartment, complete with private chapel, which is currently undergoing renovations.
This type of cancer affects both smokers and nonsmokers, although Leo is not known to ever have been a smoker.
The cancer diagnosis could complicate his busy schedule.
Just weeks earlier, hundreds of thousands of people packed the streets of Paris for an outdoor mass on a visit that saw Leo warn about the risks of artificial intelligence.
He was planning to take a historic two-week visit to South America next month, although it is unclear if that will still go ahead.
Messages of support and sympathy flowed in after the news.
Dr. Fernando Daniels III, a 67-year-old physician from Maryland  was among many praying for Leo’s swift recovery in the Vatican’s St. Peter’s Square.
“I’ve seen miracles in medicine. I’ve seen people told with terminal illnesses they wouldn’t live and they did,” he told NBC News.
“Prayers of all should heal him,” said Daniels, who was traveling as part of a group.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he and his wife, Jeanette Rubio, were praying for the pope.
“May the Lord give him strength and the Holy Spirit guide the medical professionals taking care of the Holy Father,” Rubio said on X.
“We thank God that the surgery on Pope Leo was, by all accounts, successful, and that he continues his recovery and recuperation,” New York City’s Archbishop Ronald Hicks said in a statement.
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, whose role is largely ceremonial, wished Leo a speedy and full recovery, the German Catholic news agency KNA reported.
“The pope‘s voice on the current issues and challenges of our time is of particular importance and of value to many people worldwide, including in Germany, beyond denominational boundaries,” Steinmeier was quoted as saying.
Claudio Lavanga reported from Vatican City, Mithil Aggarwal reported from Hong Kong, Corky Siemaszko reported from New York City.
Claudio Lavanga is Rome-based foreign correspondent for NBC News.
Mithil Aggarwal is a Hong Kong-based reporter/producer for NBC News.
Corky Siemaszko is a senior reporter for NBC News Digital.

articles.title_orig: Alibaba AI models cleared for use in Apple Intelligence in China just in time for the iPhone Duo launch
articles.title_zh: Alibaba AI models cleared for use in Apple Intelligence in China just in time for the iPhone Duo launch
articles.content_orig:
Apple’s integrated AI system is still yet to be rolled out in mainland China, despite launching nearly two years ago.
Apple Intelligence will soon be making its way to supported iPhone models in China, as the country reportedly rubber stamps the use of Alibaba AI models to power the technology.
As reported by the South China Morning Post , which is owned by the Alibaba Group, China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has given regulatory approval for Tongyi Qianwen, the group of LLMs better known as Qwen, as well as the Tongyi Wanxiang AI-generated image and video tool.
Apple had already received clearance to roll out Apple Intelligence on the Chinese mainland back in July, but the South China Morning Post 's report says it has not yet done so. The updated filings include network access permits for the iPhone Duo and 18 Pro , with the former set to launch in China next week with the new and improved Siri AI as one of its flagship software features.
Much of Apple Intelligence's feature set is already available in Hong Kong, but the mainland's complex AI and privacy laws have required Apple to be patient about bringing what is now a core feature to one of its fastest-growing markets. It will seemingly now arrive almost exactly two years after it launched in the US, where Apple has worked with both Google and OpenAI to train its models and hand off complex questions.
Reports that Apple would seek to work with Chinese AI firms for a workaround to bring Apple Intelligence to the country first emerged as far back as early 2025, with Alibaba named at the time. Back in the summer, it was confirmed that Qwen would be central to Apple Intelligence in compatible iPhone, iPad, Mac and Vision Pro models that it sells to its Chinese customers.

articles.title_orig: ASML’s chip equipment sales to China soar 109% despite US export curb push
articles.title_zh: ASML’s chip equipment sales to China soar 109% despite US export curb push
articles.content_orig:
The Dutch firm expects China to account for 20 per cent of its total sales this year, even as the US pushes for tighter export restrictions
Dutch semiconductor equipment giant ASML expects China to account for about 20 per cent of its total sales this year, after seeing shipments to the market more than double during the previous quarter despite mounting US pressure for tighter export restrictions on less advanced chipmaking machinery.
The company’s sales to China surged 109 per cent in the third quarter compared with the previous three months, according to financial results released on Wednesday. That took China’s share of ASML’s machine sales to 23 per cent, up from 14 per cent in the second quarter.
The revenue jump comes as Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten faces pressure from Washington to tighten restrictions on sales of chipmaking machines to China.

articles.title_orig: China elevates ties with Botswana and Togo
articles.title_zh: China elevates ties with Botswana and Togo
articles.content_orig:
At the invitation of President Xi Jinping, President of the Republic of Botswana Duma Gideon Boko paid a state visit to China from October 12 to 17.
Xi Jinping held talks with his Botswanan counterpart in Beijing’s Great Hall of the People on the afternoon of October 13. The two heads of state made the announcement to elevate their bilateral relationship to a comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership.
President Xi noted that Botswana voted in support of restoring the People’s Republic of China’s lawful seat in the United Nations in the 1970s, even before the two countries established diplomatic ties. Today, the two countries are marching side by side on the journey toward modernisation, writing a new chapter in bilateral friendship. China-Botswana friendship should shine bright and endure like diamonds. (Botswana ranks second in world diamond production after the Russian Federation.)
Xi further observed that a common direction brings people together on the same road. This year marks the 105th anniversary of the founding of the Communist Party of China and the 60th anniversary of the independence of Botswana. The two governing parties should strengthen cooperation, deepen experience-sharing in state governance, and foster greater convergence of ideas. (President Boko heads the Umbrella for Democratic Change, an alliance of left-wing parties including the Botswana National Front, the Botswana Movement for Democracy, the Botswana People’s Party and the Botswana Congress Party. It achieved a landslide victory in the 2024 elections, forming the first left-wing government in the country’s history.)
China, Xi added, supports Botswana in pursuing a development path suited to its national conditions. The two sides should continue to develop the framework for economic and trade cooperation and seize the new opportunities emerging from China’s zero-tariff treatment for African countries having diplomatic relations with China. China is ready to enhance cooperation with Botswana in areas such as the digital economy, agriculture and the livestock industry and carry out the Smart Education Project to support economic and social development in Botswana.
Xi put forward a four-point proposition on China-Botswana and China-Africa mining cooperation:
First, the starting principle should be African resources belonging to Africa. China stands ready to share its experience and help African countries formulate mining development plans consistent with their national conditions.
Second, the guiding philosophy should be a right approach to friendship and interests and ensuring mutual benefit. China will continue to encourage Chinese companies to enhance their operational capacity, transfer green technologies suited to Africa’s conditions, and promote South-South cooperation in mining development.
Third, the direction of cooperation should be high-quality development. China will continue to move China-Africa mining cooperation toward industrial value addition, explore new financing models that are affordable and sustainable, and support Africa’s modernisation through high-standard cooperation.
Fourth, a fair and open cooperation environment is crucial. Africa’s resources should not be used for geopolitical rivalry. China would be glad to see other parties providing genuine support for Africa’s development and stands ready to work with Africa to create more enabling conditions for business investment and operation.
President Boko said that under President Xi Jinping’s strong leadership, China has made remarkable development achievements. China has lifted all its people out of poverty and opened a successful development path with Chinese characteristics, which is a good example for Botswana to follow.
He added that Botswana attaches great importance to its relations with China, will stay committed to the one-China principle, oppose any separatist attempt to seek “Taiwan independence,” and oppose any interference in China’s internal affairs. His country welcomes more Chinese companies to invest and operate in Botswana, so as to enhance cooperation under the Belt and Road Initiative and work together in industrial development, agriculture, mining, innovation, and digital transformation to deliver more tangible outcomes in bilateral relations.
The two countries agreed a Joint Statement on the Establishment of a Comprehensive Strategic Cooperative Partnership.
In it, the two sides shared the assessment that the world is undergoing an accelerating transformation, characterised by heightened geopolitical tensions, economic uncertainty, rapid technological change and increasingly complex global challenges. Botswana highly commended President Xi Jinping’s proposals, including the building of a community with a shared future for humanity and high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, which are conducive to bringing valuable stability to a turbulent world.
It added: “In this context, the two Presidents decided to elevate bilateral relations to a Comprehensive Strategic Cooperative Partnership between the People’s Republic of China and the Republic of Botswana, opening a new chapter in the longstanding and evolving relationship between the two countries.”
They further recognised the important contribution of political-party exchanges to enhancing mutual understanding and promoting people-centred governance. They agreed to encourage exchanges and experience-sharing between their respective political parties in areas including leadership development, policy formulation, organisational development, training and institutional strengthening. Botswana welcomed opportunities for members of the Umbrella for Democratic Change to participate in relevant bilateral and multilateral training and capacity-building programmes hosted by China.
The statement is noteworthy in that it details ways of working together to advance the four key global initiatives put forward by China.
On the Global Development Initiative (GDI), Botswana welcomed measures aimed at expanding market access and strengthening China–Africa economic and trade relations, including the zero-tariff measures for the 53 African countries having diplomatic relations with China initiated by President Xi Jinping. In this regard, they agreed to work together to expand bilateral trade and facilitate greater access for Botswana’s products to the Chinese market, including through the effective utilisation of Green Channel 2.0 and other appropriate trade facilitation mechanisms. The two sides committed to expanding market opportunities for Botswana’s beef, citrus and other agricultural products, while working to address relevant technical, sanitary, phytosanitary and market-access requirements.
The two sides also reaffirmed their shared commitment to strengthening China-Africa solidarity, unity and cooperation in pursuit of common development, peace and prosperity. They recognised the strategic importance of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) as a key platform for collective dialogue, policy coordination and practical cooperation between China and African countries. They welcomed the 70th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Africa and agreed to work together to advance the outcomes and commitments of FOCAC.
On the Global Security Initiative (GSI), they committed to strengthening exchanges and practical cooperation in support of peace and security in Africa and to contributing, within their respective capacities, to international and regional peace, security and stability. They reaffirmed their support for the principle of “African solutions to African problems” and agreed that African countries and institutions should play the leading role in preventing and resolving conflicts on the continent. They expressed support for the African Union and regional economic communities in their efforts to prevent and resolve conflicts, promote dialogue and strengthen peace and security.

articles.title_orig: Seeking Gospel hope in a world increasingly shaped by AI
articles.title_zh: Seeking Gospel hope in a world increasingly shaped by AI
articles.content_orig:
Author: Br. Steven Patti, OFM
Date Published: October 14, 2026
How can we stay rooted in the dignity of the human person amid rapidly advancing technology? Br. Steven Patti, OFM, recently considered that question with parishioners at St. Camillus Church in Silver Spring, Maryland, during a series of discussions on Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical Magnifica Humanitas. In this reflection, Br. Steven shares what they discerned about AI, human dignity and the hope found in the Gospel.
Br. Jorge Hernandez, OFM, pastor of St. Camillus Church, asked me if I would give a reflection on Pope Leo’s recent encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas. And so, for three successive Saturdays in September, for two hours each session, a group of us met in the Francis Room to discuss the encyclical, with chairs set up in a circle around the room.
Most had heard about the encyclical, but few, if any, had read it. They were curious and interested in learning more. We looked at several questions: What is an encyclical? What is Leo doing in this encyclical? What did we find in it over our three sessions?
Magnifica Humanitas is lengthy, and much of it is rooted in the Bible and in Catholic Social Teaching. Leo XIV refers to his predecessor in name, Leo XIII, and to Leo’s Rerum Novarum, which addressed the rising industrialization of the late 19th century. We talked about how it was no accident that our modern Leo chose his papal name: Both popes show a deep concern for the centrality of the human person amid rising industrialization and technology, 135 years apart.
Br. Steven Patti, OFM, said participants in a discussion about Magnifica Humanitas expressed concern about the fate of humans, given the rapid rise of artificial intelligence. (Photo courtesy of Br. Steven)
This resonated with people. The group expressed fears: What is happening to our world around us? Where is, and what is the fate of, “the person,” the human person, amid an emerging world of AI? What and whom can I trust amid rising disinformation, surveillance and data collection, and AI as a social companion? What does it mean when AI gives answers without any authentic sense or knowledge of mercy and compassion? What does AI mean for the future of warfare?
‘Humanity at risk’ was a common topic of conversation among the group, along with a sense that the human person is increasingly becoming a cog in a machine. There was also a sense of gratitude for the pope’s words, for his speaking publicly and prophetically about an issue that seems to develop in new ways daily.
In the discussions Br. Steven Patti, OFM, led, he mentioned that Pope Leo XIV reminds us who we are called to be during a social shift that can at times feel baffling and confusing. (Photo courtesy of Br. Steven)
But the news was not all grim. Even amid an ever-changing technological landscape, Magnifica Humanitas points to the Gospel, to who we are as disciples of Christ in our modern world. Leo reminds us who we are called to be amid this often bewildering and disorienting social change.
He writes beautifully and with hope: “Even in the darkest nights, the Lord raises up men and women who refuse to give up, who persevere in doing good, who protect the vulnerable and open pathways to reconciliation” (MH 211). He adds, “Do not think that the problems are too big, and that we are too small” (MH 212).
And so, what did we find after three Saturday morning sessions?
It felt like modern Church: a naming of the signs of the times, shared voices around the circle, and a shared sense that the Gospel and our entire Christian tradition root us in the centrality and dignity of the human person and in how we are called to follow in the footsteps of Jesus.
As Pope Leo ends his encyclical: “With the same faith as Mary, let us become weavers of hope in our world, sharing who we are and what we have, so that the presence of Jesus may grow among us and his kingdom take shape” (MH 245).

articles.title_orig: Real-World Data Expand Evidence for Mogamulizumab in CTCL
articles.title_zh: Real-World Data Expand Evidence for Mogamulizumab in CTCL
articles.content_orig:
Real-world German MINT data show mogamulizumab delivers durable responses, ~20-month PFS, manageable safety, and improved quality of life in MF and Sézary syndrome.
Mogamulizumab (Poteligeo) was associated with durable real-world treatment outcomes in patients with mycosis fungoides (MF) and Sézary syndrome (SS), according to final results from the German MINT study. 1
In this real-world analysis, treatment with mogamulizumab was associated with an overall response rate of 62.4% and a median progression-free survival (PFS) of 20.2 months. Among 109 patients, the median time to next treatment was 14.9 months, providing additional data on treatment duration in routine clinical practice.
“For patients living with [MF] and [SS], understanding how treatments perform outside the controlled setting of clinical trials is critically important,” Chalif Assad, MD, of Helios Klinikum Krefeld, Health and Medical University Düsseldorf-Krefeld in Germany, stated in a news release. “The final MINT results demonstrate meaningful clinical outcomes across a broad patient population treated in routine practice and highlight the value of collaborative real-world research in helping clinicians make informed treatment decisions.”
MINT (Mogamulizumab in a Non-interventional Study to Evaluate the Safety and Outcome in Mycosis Fungoides and Sézary Syndrome Treatment) was a multicenter, noninterventional study conducted at 18 centers across Germany. The analysis included 56 patients with MF and 53 with SS, with a median follow-up of 25.2 months. Most patients (83.5%) had advanced disease, defined as stage IIB or higher, at treatment initiation.
Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 38.5% of patients, with drug eruption and lymphopenia among the most commonly reported events. Serious TRAEs leading to treatment discontinuation occurred in 22.0% of patients. The overall safety profile was described as consistent with findings from the phase 3 MAVORIC trial (NCT01728805), which supported mogamulizumab’s FDA approval in CTCL in August 2018. 2
Quality of life improved during treatment, with median Skindex-29 scores decreasing from 49.1 at baseline (n = 21) to 30.2 at month 12 (n = 7), representing a 38.5% improvement. However, the small number of patients with available month 12 assessments limits interpretation of this finding.
The MINT findings complement results from MAVORIC, which compared mogamulizumab with vorinostat (Zolinza) in 372 patients with previously treated MF or SS. In MAVORIC, median PFS was 7.7 months with mogamulizumab vs 3.1 months with vorinostat (HR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.41-0.69; P <.0001). 3
Together, the studies contribute to the evidence base for mogamulizumab in MF and SS, with MINT extending observations to a real-world population that included a high proportion of patients with advanced disease. However, the observational design and limited sample sizes in certain subgroups underscore the need for caution when interpreting these findings.

articles.title_orig: Cochlear Named #1 Most Trustworthy Healthcare Company In The World For 2026
articles.title_zh: Cochlear Named #1 Most Trustworthy Healthcare Company In The World For 2026
articles.content_orig:
Newsweek's World's Most Trustworthy Companies 2026 Ranks Cochlear as Top Healthcare & Life Sciences Company
LONE TREE, Colo. , Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cochlear, the global leader in implantable hearing solutions, is proud to announce that it has been ranked No. 1 in the Health Care & Life Sciences industry by Newsweek in its World's Most Trustworthy Companies 2026 rankings. This marks the second time in three years that Cochlear has earned this prestigious recognition, reinforcing Cochlear's commitment to excellence, innovation, and a recipient first mindset.
The Newsweek ranking was conducted independently in collaboration with global data research firm Statista and evaluated companies on the trust they inspire among customers, investors, and employees. The 2026 edition is based on approximately 200,000 company evaluations from more than 65,000 participants across 20 countries, complemented by an analysis of over 320,000 media mentions, providing a comprehensive global view of organizations distinguished by strong reputations, resilience, and lasting stakeholder trust.
"At Cochlear, our recipients and candidates are at the heart of everything we do. This recognition from Newsweek reflects the dedication of every person across our organization who works tirelessly to support people with hearing loss throughout their entire hearing journey," said Dig Howitt, Chief Executive Officer & President, Cochlear.
"It also reflects our longstanding commitment to earning the trust of those we serve through the quality, reliability, and innovation of our hearing solutions. Every day, we work to provide the best possible outcomes and technology that recipients and professionals can rely on for a lifetime of hearing outcomes. This accolade highlights the dedication to our mission to help people hear and be heard."
About Cochlear Limited (ASX: COH)
People have always been Cochlear's inspiration, ever since Professor Graeme Clark set out to create the first multi-channel cochlear implant after seeing his father struggle with hearing loss. Since 1981, Cochlear has helped more than 800,000 people of all ages in more than 180 countries to hear. As the global leader in implantable hearing solutions, Cochlear connects people with life's opportunities, and welcomes them to the world's largest hearing implant community.
Cochlear has a global workforce of more than 5,500 people with a passion for progress, who strive to meet the needs of people living with hearing loss. The company continually innovates to anticipate future needs, investing more than A$3 billion to date in research and development to push the boundaries of technology and help more people hear.

articles.title_orig: OpenAI engineer arrested after recording device found at San Francisco office
articles.title_zh: OpenAI engineer arrested after recording device found at San Francisco office
articles.content_orig:
Palantir settled a lawsuit over the London mayor's office deciding to block a $66 million contract between the tech firm and the city's police department, Reuters reported.
Palantir had agreed to a two-year-deal with the London Metropolitan Police to use its artificial intelligence systems to analyze evidence and streamline certain tasks.
Mayor Sadiq Khan's office stopped the agreement from being implemented, accusing the Metro Police of not holding open competition for the contract. A spokesperson for Khan also said that Palantir did not align with "London's values," according to Reuters.
On Wednesday, Palantir and the Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime (MOPAC) said they had resolved the case and were withdrawing their allegations against each other.
Palantir is now welcome to participate in any future contracts, according to a joint statement from the company and MOPAC.
Reuters contributed to this post.
OpenAI said a former employee took over 100 "highly confidential files" about at least one unreleased device while still employed and later presented the company's product plans to senior leadership at Apple, according to a new filing in the lawsuit between OpenAI and Apple.
The employee, who left OpenAI for Apple , sent the files to his personal accounts on June 2, his last day at the company, according to the Tuesday filing in federal court in San Jose, California .
The files included "detailed images" of the unreleased device, supplier information and other trade secrets, according to OpenAI's lawyers.
The employee then gave a presentation about this device to higher-ups at Apple, including vice president of operations in Asia, the filing said. The presentation, OpenAI said, happened months ago.
"OpenAI is very concerned that its trade secret and confidential information is now circulating inside Apple, where Apple engineers can shape Apple’s upcoming products based on OpenAI’s confidential and innovative work," OpenAI's lawyers wrote.
They continued: "OpenAI has raised these issues directly with Apple, but to date, Apple has not provided OpenAI with the requested assurances that Apple is not in possession of, and has not used, OpenAI’s trade secret and confidential information."
Apple told Fox News Digital that it found no evidence to support OpenAI's allegations, accusing the company of trying to distract from claims that it stole Apple's confidential information.
Apple said that it has told OpenAI it would work with them to find any information that was possibly taken. Apple added, at this time, it has not found any proprietary data on its systems after searching for the one file OpenAI identified.
Apple also said OpenAI did not respond to a request for more information to help the internal investigation.
A woman in Russia’s Far East was fined this week after an AI-generated image of a bear that she sent to a friend spread through the community, alarming residents already on edge over increased bear activity in the region.
The resident of Magdagachi settlement, ​Amur region, used ChatGPT in September to create the image of a large bear walking down a local street before sending it to her friend, Reuters reported.
The image was then shared through various messaging apps, prompting residents to make dozens of alarmed calls to the police.
The woman confessed to creating and sending the image, saying it was meant to be a prank. A court fined her 15,000 ‌roubles ($178) this week, according to Reuters.
At least 26 people have been killed in bear attacks across Russia since the animals emerged from hibernation this spring, Russian state news agency RIA Novosti reported Monday.
Reuters contributed to this report.
Some 33% of Virginia's 80 state agencies reported using at least one function-specific AI tool in their daily workflows, according to research commissioned by the state senate.
Another 30% said they were considering adopting AI , while 38% reported no current use of the technology.
Virginia Joint Legislative Audit and Review Commission, which released the report, recommended updating Virginia's AI standards, introducing risk-based oversight and requiring annual AI training for state employees.
President Donald Trump's top science advisor, Michael Kratsios, said the United States is four to six months ahead of China in the artificial intelligence race .
During an appearance Wednesday morning on Fox Business's 'Big Money in the Morning,' Kratsios also addressed a recent warning by Anthropic that advanced AI models could soon infect internet-connected devices in people's homes.
"I think we always have to be vigilant and think very carefully about the cyber risk presented with new technologies, and I think that's one of the core cruxes of the superintelligence task force," Kratsios said. "We want to make sure that we're leading the world in SI, but at the same time making sure that we're on top of and monitoring these national security threats to the country."
Anthropic said Wednesday it will be opening an office in Singapore after it signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with the island nation.
The MOU sets out "areas of cooperation in AI safety, security, and model evaluation; research on AI adoption and its impact; and responsible adoption across the public and private sectors," according to Anthropic.
The Singapore office is Anthropic's fifth location in the Asia Pacific region. The company's other offices are located in Tokyo, Japan; Bengaluru, India; Seoul, South Korea; and Sydney, Australia.
Britain's media regulator Ofcom said on Wednesday that it had placed new restrictions on Grok, the chatbot created by Elon Musk's SpaceXAI, formerly xAI.
Users in Britain are no longer allowed to use Grok to view, generate or share pornographic content, Ofcom said.
Companion chatbots, include the anime-inspired "Ani," are also banned from engaging in sexually-explicit conversations with users.
Earlier this year, Ofcom began investigating reports of Grok being used to create sexual deepfakes of real individuals
Nvidia announced Tuesday that it will invest $10 billion in four artificial intelligence firms based in France .
The companies include Doctolib, Entalpic, Genesis AI and Pigment.
Doctolib develops AI agents for healthcare providers and patients; Entalpic uses AI to develop advanced materials for semiconductors and electronics; Genesis AI is building general-purpose robots; and Pigment offers AI-powered business planning and forecasting software.
An adversary can interrupt an artificial intelligence system without defeating its software. It need only strike the infrastructure that keeps the system running. Ukraine proved the point inside Russia this past week.
President Trump and his national security team should take note before an enemy tries the same thing here. On October 8, a Ukrainian drone attack forced Yandex, the technology company often called "Russia’s Google," to suspend operations at its Sasovo data center. The next day, another strike knocked out several modules at its Kaluga facility, which Yandex had called its most powerful data center in Russia . On October 11, the company announced that its Vladimir-region data center had shut down completely after a drone attack. Ukraine disrupted three major Yandex computing facilities in four days.
The Sasovo facility housed two of Yandex’s three supercomputers used to train its AI models, including YandexGPT. Yandex said it could not yet determine whether the equipment could be restored. Whatever the final damage assessment, Russia’s leading AI developer lost a major computing hub in a single night.
During my years as an Army officer and Pentagon strategist, I learned to judge a military capability by whether it would be there when needed. A weapon that dazzles on the test range becomes a liability when its supply line fails in combat.
That standard should govern our dependence on AI.
